Background: Riverside Community Garden has 40 plots, allocated by a volunteer with paper forms/wall chart per season March to October.

1 Apply for coming season choosing up to three preferred plots.
2 Coordinator allocates from applications and moves unallocated applicants to waiting list in application order.
3 Gardener sees their allocated plot and season dates.
4 Gardener reports a problem with their plot; coordinator sees open reports and marks resolved.
5 Coordinator sees grid of 40 plots with holders.
Rules: at most one plot per household per season; last-season holders who apply before 1 February allocated before new applicants; waiting list strictly first come first served.
Later: online payment, tool lending excluded.
Constraints: phone usable, contact details coordinator only, large text/plain language.
Open: sign-in, report notifications.
Owner conversation: sign-in emailed one-time link, no passwords. Coordinator one daily email listing new reports. Technology no preference. Other unresolved matters use agent judgement. Do not reask answered material.

Daily digest at configurable local time default 09:00, no email on empty day, includes newly reported items even if since resolved; failures retained for catch-up. # Plotbook -- community garden plot booking
Background: Riverside Community Garden has 40 plots, allocated by a volunteer with paper forms/wall chart per season March to October.
Users: about 60 gardener households apply, see allocation, report plot problems; one coordinator reviews, allocates, manages waiting list, resolves problems.
First version must:
1 Apply for coming season choosing up to three preferred plots.
2 Coordinator allocates from applications and moves unallocated applicants to waiting list in application order.
3 Gardener sees their allocated plot and season dates.
4 Gardener reports a problem with their plot; coordinator sees open reports and marks resolved.
5 Coordinator sees grid of 40 plots with holders.
Rules: at most one plot per household per season; last-season holders who apply before 1 February allocated before new applicants; waiting list strictly first come first served.
Later: online payment, tool lending excluded.
Constraints: phone usable, contact details coordinator only, large text/plain language.
Open: sign-in, report notifications.
Owner conversation: sign-in emailed one-time link, no passwords. Coordinator one daily email listing new reports. Technology no preference. Other unresolved matters use agent judgement. Do not reask answered material.

Discovery: only brief.md, no code, manifests, tests, git or .story; no verified completed capabilities.
Product acceptance: complete phone application-to-allocation-to-report journey; coordinator manages 40 plots and fair queue, receives daily digest; privacy isolation; all three allocation rules verified.
Proposed architecture (not existing): Python/Django server-rendered HTML/CSS with minimal JavaScript, PostgreSQL; standard email transport interface and scheduled Django command. Hosting/email supplier selected in P01 after feasibility check, paid purchases not part of setup.
Assumptions to approve: one email login represents one household; coordinator can reconcile duplicate household records before allocation (do not infer household by email alone); household identity persisted independently of email. Preferences optional (0-3 distinct plots), ordered but not guarantees. Season dates default March 1-October 31, coordinator editable within March-October. Garden timezone must be configured before dated allocation; eligible returning deadline exclusive Feb 1 00:00 garden local time. Returning priority applies initial allocation only; after waiting list finalization its global application-order queue takes precedence. Within priority group use application timestamp then stable ID; late returning applicants enter ordinary initial pool. Initial allocation and waiting-list finalization open only at or after February 1 00:00 of the season year in garden local time. Every active eligible timely returner must receive an available plot before any ordinary applicant. A reason or waitlisted status never bypasses this guard. Returning applicants can withdraw explicitly, with audit; if eligible returners exceed capacity no ordinary applicant receives a plot. Within returners, application order resolves oversubscription. Only once capacity is exhausted or all active applicants have allocations may the initial round finalize; the remaining applications then enter global FIFO order. This does not reserve the previous plot. No automated application expiry. Queue retains original submitted_at, edits cannot jump queue. Coordinator assigns available plots manually, preferences advisory, waiting list only head allocated, no arbitrary overrides. Correction/release audit required. Daily digest at configurable local time default 09:00, send an explicit no-new-reports summary on empty days, includes newly reported items even if since resolved; failures retained for catch-up. A durable batch/provider idempotency strategy must avoid duplicate daily delivery under retries; provider capabilities verified before release.
Open operational dependencies: verified sender and coordinator email, garden timezone, household reconciliation and last-season paper records, plot labels/layout. No business rule silently deferred. Synthetic fixtures for development; no real contact data in repository.
